known.name: mHC (manifold-constrained hyper-connections)
known.mechanism: Projects the HC residual mixing matrix onto doubly stochastic matrices (Birkhoff polytope) with Sinkhorn-Knopp, 20 iterations by default, and keeps the pre and post maps non-negative, to restore identity-mapping stability.
known.effect: The authors report better stability and scaling than unconstrained HC at negligible overhead, using fused kernels, recomputation and DualPipe overlap. I could not read the ablation numbers: only the abstract and secondary summaries were readable.
known.where: DeepSeek large-scale MoE models; expansion rate 4

known.name: Hyper-Connections (static vs dynamic)
known.mechanism: Replaces the residual with n parallel streams and learned depth and width connection weights, either static (SHC) or token-dependent (DHC).
known.effect: At expansion rate 2, SHC and DHC give similar gains. At rate 4, DHC is clearly better: OLMo-1B V2 eval loss is 2.781 for dynamic ×4 against 2.791 for static ×4. At n=1, DHC is worse than the baseline.
known.where: OLMo-1B and MoE models, expansion rates 1, 2 and 4

known.name: Frac-Connections
known.mechanism: Splits the hidden state into fractions instead of replicating it, which gives HC-like multi-stream mixing with less memory.
known.effect: The dynamic variant (DFC×4) beats the static one (SFC×4), the same pattern as in HC.

known.name: MUDDFormer (multiway dynamic dense connections)
known.mechanism: Computes dense cross-layer connection weights dynamically per position, with separate streams for Q, K, V and the residual.
known.effect: An ablation on a 405M model shows that static, dynamic and multiway dense connections each contribute to performance.
known.where: Models up to about 405M and larger

known.name: mHC-lite
known.mechanism: Builds exactly doubly stochastic matrices as convex combinations of permutation matrices (Birkhoff–von Neumann), so no Sinkhorn iterations are needed.
known.effect: Matches or exceeds mHC, has higher throughput with a naive implementation, and removes the instabilities seen in HC and mHC. The authors argue finite Sinkhorn leaves approximation error that accumulates with depth.
known.where: Small and medium language models. The abstract gave no numbers.

known.name: sHC (Spectral-Sphere-Constrained Hyper-Connections)
known.mechanism: Replaces the Birkhoff polytope with a spectral-norm sphere, which allows negative entries and avoids Sinkhorn.
known.effect: The authors say mHC matrices collapse toward identity, and that non-negativity blocks subtractive mixing. In the appendix, composite column sums are 1.00 across depth for sHC, against 0.11 to 3.11 for mHC.
known.where: Language models. I did not see the benchmark numbers.

known.name: Stream collapse analysis and symmetry-breaking initialization
known.mechanism: Breaks symmetry among streams at initialization (the LSS variant) to stop one stream from dominating the write operator and norm growth.
known.effect: After an early phase the mixing matrix stays near identity and one stream's norm dominates in deep layers. Symmetry-breaking init reduces the imbalance and improves results across mHC variants.

known.name: Small nanoGPT-scale mHC variants (go-mHC, TBP-mHC)
known.mechanism: Alternative parameterizations of the doubly stochastic mixing: generalized orthostochastic matrices (go-mHC) and transportation polytopes (TBP-mHC).
known.effect: go-mHC, mHC-lite and KromHC perform about the same on a 30M, 6-layer nanoGPT, so the result is parity and not an advantage. TBP-mHC was tested at 6 layers × 512 and 12 layers × 768 on OpenWebText for 10k iterations, with KromHC runs excluded for gradient instability.
known.where: 30M nanoGPT on TinyStories; OpenWebText at 6×512 and 12×768

known.name: modded-nanogpt skip, value-embedding and U-net residual shortcuts
known.mechanism: Adds learned-scale skip connections from the embedding to each block, U-net-pattern layer skips, and value embeddings mixed into attention values, with gating on later versions.
known.effect: In the speedrun log, value and embedding skips arrived at 8.2 min, U-net skips at 7.2 min, and U-net value embeddings at 3.95 min. The README also notes that the residual stream decays exponentially.

failed.name: Dynamic HC at expansion rate 1
failed.why: DHC with n=1 is worse than the baseline. Gains only appear for n>1, and dynamic beats static mainly at n=4.

failed.name: Birkhoff-constrained mixing staying at identity
failed.why: Learned mHC matrices drift back toward identity, which gives little cross-stream exchange. Non-negativity blocks subtractive mixing, and finite Sinkhorn is only approximately doubly stochastic, with composite column sums from 0.11 to 3.11 across depth.

failed.name: Fancier doubly stochastic parameterizations at tiny scale
failed.why: go-mHC, mHC-lite and KromHC show only parity on a 30M nanoGPT, so a better parameterization of the mixing alone did not help at small scale. The authors cite limited compute.

open.direction: Symmetry-breaking stream initialization instead of identical copies, to prevent one stream from dominating
open.why: The stream-collapse paper shows that identical streams with near-identity mixing become a single dominant stream. Whether this holds at 21M and 50M tokens is untested.

open.direction: Mixing matrices that allow negative entries (spectral-sphere or orthogonal, for example SO(4) via quaternions) in place of Sinkhorn
open.why: This removes the non-negativity limit and the Sinkhorn cost, and gives exact norm control. It has not been compared with mHC at small scale.

open.direction: Full-expressivity polytope parameterizations (transportation polytopes) of the mixing
open.why: Standard mHC cannot represent every useful mixing. A cheaper exact parameterization might replace 20 Sinkhorn iterations at no loss.

open.direction: Token-dependent read and write weights at expansion rate 4, with static doubly stochastic residual mixing kept
open.why: Dynamic weights beat static ones at n=4 in HC and MUDD, but the combination with a constrained mixing matrix has not been tested at small scale.

open.direction: Gated embedding and value-embedding skips combined with multi-stream mixing
open.why: The speedrun gains from embedding skips, U-net skips and gated value embeddings were found with a single stream. Their interaction with multi-stream mixing is unexplored.
